obtained.how: agency copy: USGS Publications Warehouse PDF of Open-File Report 2010-1214 (text layer; the West Grand table checked against its page image)

bibliography.checked_against: the report's title page and suggested citation (PDF pp. 3–4) and Crossref
bibliography.note: Hodgkins, G.A., 2010, Historical ice-out dates for 29 lakes in New England, 1807–2008: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 2010–1214, 32 p. The report tabulates ice-out as Julian day per year (Tables 1–29) and gives no statistics: every mean, SD and extreme in the paper is project arithmetic, recomputed here from the tables (script: Julian day → date on a 365-day year for means, the actual year for extremes).

claims.claim: West Grand Lake ice-out averaged 24 April over 1979–2008
claims.conditions: n = 30 years (1979–2008), mean Julian day 113.8 (= 23.8 April), SD 9.0; single family of observers (Staples) for the whole record

claims.claim: West Grand Lake (45.2° N): mean ice-out 28 April over 1878–2008, SD 8.8 days, extremes 2 April – 19 May
claims.quote: Period of record—1878 to 2008 Years of record—131
claims.conditions: 131 years, mean Julian day 118.42 (28 April), SD 8.75; earliest 92 (2 April 2006), latest 139 (19 May 1918); latitude 45°12'56"

claims.note: The table's empty 'Record' cells can be filled: Sebec 1879–2008, Portage 1925–2008 (and Squa Pan 1930–2008, Sebago 1807–2008).

claims.claim: Squa Pan (46.6° N): mean 2 May, SD 7.0, extremes 13 Apr – 18 May, 30 Apr (1979–2008)
claims.source_value: latest ice-out was Julian day 138 in 1972, a leap year: 17 May, not 18 May (mean 122.5 = 2 May, SD 6.98, earliest 103 = 13 April 1945, 1979–2008 mean 120.56 = 30 April all hold)
claims.note: A one-day slip from converting a leap-year Julian day on a 365-day calendar.

claims.claim: Sebago (southern Maine): mean ice-out 16 April; ~6 April over 1979–2008
claims.quote: [--, no data; NCIC, no complete ice cover]
claims.conditions: 158 years with an ice-out date (1807–2008) mean 106.44 (16 April); 1979–2008 n = 26, mean 96.54 (6.5 April)
claims.note: Means exclude the years of no complete ice cover ('NCIC': 10 years in the record, 4 of them in 1979–2008: 1991, 1998, 1999, 2002), so they describe ice years only and are biased late; worth a footnote.

claims.claim: farther north (46.6–47.0° N), mean ice-out comes 4–11 days later than at West Grand (Table 3.1-2)
claims.conditions: differences from West Grand: each lake's own full-record mean 4.1 (Squa Pan), 8.2 (Portage), 8.5 d (Eagle); 1979–2008 means 6.8, 9.5, 11.4 d; paired over the same years (each northern lake's full record) 5.6, 9.7, 10.5 d
claims.note: '4–11' spans figures from different periods (Squa Pan's long-term 4 d, Eagle's recent 11 d). Like for like: 4–9 d (full records), 7–11 d (1979–2008), or ~6–10 d paired by year, the cleanest statement.

notes: The quotes for the row claims are the tables' record headers; the values are recomputed from the Julian-day columns (raw text parsed by script and spot-checked against the page image of Table 28). Hodgkins (2010) updates Hodgkins & James (2002, OFR 02-34) through 2008; definitions of ice-out vary by observer and are 'not known with confidence in most cases' (p. 3), and one year each was excluded at China, Damariscotta, Portage and Sebec Lakes (two at Messalonskee). The '~20 Apr (2015–26)' West Grand mean and the East Grand row are from Maine BPL, not this report.
